Subject: Vendor portal: identity-claim + PO field exception (MSA redline impact)

Hi team — thanks again for walking through the onboarding checklist this morning. Two items came up that I want to capture in one place so we can align actions and owners. Attached are our working redline (Acme_MSA_redline_20280530.pdf) and a short PO schema notes workbook that highlights the field mismatch (Acme_PO_schema_notes.xlsx).

1) Identity-proofing / identity-claim: Acme's procurement team is requesting that vendors complete an "identity-claim" step (tax ID + authorized signer proof) during portal registration. That would change the current self-serve flow in Ariba and could block our usual fast-path onboarding. Can you confirm whether your portal team can accept a vendor attestation + KYC snapshot instead of a full identity re-assertion at registration? If not, we'll need a short-term manual verification run for this cohort.

2) PO field mismatch: Acme requires an additional buyer_reference field and a non-standard taxCode element in line items. Our Order Form (and the MSA) currently assume normalized PO fields; altering them affects how our EDI/Ariba mapping works and may conflict with the attached MSA redline where Acme requested changes to the invoice acceptance language.

Requested next steps:
- Can Acme contracts confirm whether the requested MSA edits in the indemnity and invoice acceptance paragraphs are deal-breakers or negotiable? (see page 3 of the redline)
- If legal is okay to proceed with a negotiated carve, we need vendor-ops/portal to confirm mapping approach and a proposed ETA for implementing the new fields in a staging Ariba tenant.

I'll loop in our legal and vendor-ops folks internally once I have simple "yes/no" guidance from contracts. Happy to jump on a 30m call if that's faster.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Partnerships (Vendor Onboarding)
Redwood Inference

Hi Naomi — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. See our initial responses below; we've attached a redline with comments (Acme_MSA_response_redline.pdf).

On identity-claim: we can accept a vendor attestation and KYC snapshot for onboarding as a temporary mitigation, provided Redwood commits to completing full identity proofing before production invoice acceptance. We want that in writing (either a short addendum to the order form or a DocuSign statement).

On PO fields: the buyer_reference is a required header for our AP system. We cannot remove it. The taxCode element is mandatory for certain line items; however, for early-stage pilots we can treat taxCode as optional if the vendor supplies a taxable-status override on the invoice. That said, the MSA edits you proposed to invoice acceptance (page 3) may limit Acme's ability to enforce payment gating tied to tax reconciliation. Legal is therefore flagging the invoice acceptance paragraph as high risk.

Two clarifying Qs for Redwood:
- Can Redwood supply an EDI mapping table that includes the proposed buyer_reference and taxCode handling to share with our Ariba team?
- Is Redwood willing to sign a short-term orderform addendum that requires full identity proofing before we enable auto-pay in production?

Proposed immediate path:
1) Sign an orderform addendum (DocuSign link included below) to allow staged onboarding with manual invoice review.
2) Work with vendor-portal@ariba.com to open a staging mapping ticket for buyer_reference / taxCode.

DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/link/ACME-ADDENDUM-2028
Attached: Acme_MSA_response_redline.pdf

Best,
